'''Simon John Bending''', {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|sep=,|FInstP}} (born 29 October 1957) is a British physicist. He is a [[professor]] in the Department of Physics at the [[University of Bath]], where he was the Head of department from 2013 to 2016.<ref name="SB10">[https://researchportal.bath.ac.uk/en/persons/simon-bending Prof Simon Bending University of Bath profile]</ref> He is co-director of the Bath-Exeter Centre for Graphene Science<ref>[https://gow.epsrc.ukri.org/NGBOViewGrant.aspx?GrantRef=EP/G036101/1 EPSRC grant details]</ref><ref>[https://www.exeter.ac.uk/news/research/title_251596_en.html University of Exeter press release]</ref> and 
deputy director of the Bath-Bristol EPRSC Centre for Doctoral Training in Condensed Matter Physics.<ref>[https://www.cdt-cmp.ac.uk/people/team/ The CDR-CMP team]</ref><ref>[https://gow.epsrc.ukri.org/NGBOViewGrant.aspx?GrantRef=EP/L015544/1 EPSRC grant details]</ref> He developed [[scanning Hall probe microscopy]]<ref name="SB1" /> and has made notable contributions to the field of [[superconductors]].<ref name="SB2" /><ref name="SB3" /><ref name="SB4" /><ref name="SB5" /><ref name="SB6" /><ref name="SB7" />

==Early life and education==
Bending  was born in [[Brentwood, Essex]] 29 October 1957 and attended St Peter's School,<ref>[https://www.stpeterssouthweald.org/ St Peter's School]</ref> in South Weald,  from 1962 to 1969 and then [[King Edward VI Grammar School, Chelmsford]] from 1969 to 1976. In 1979, he graduated B.A. Hons (1st. class) in Natural Sciences - Physics from the [[University of Cambridge]]. He obtained his PhD in 1985, from the Applied Physics Department at [[Stanford University]].<ref name="SB10" />

== Research ==
Following his PhD, Bending joined the group of Dr P. Guéret at [[IBM Research#Switzerland|IBM Research Laboratories, Zürich]], Switzerland, as a postdoc, in 1985. In 1986, he became a postdoc in the group of Prof. [[Klaus von Klitzing]], at the [[Max Planck Institut]] FKF, in Stuttgart, Germany. An year earlier, Von Klitzing had been awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Physics|Physics Nobel Prize]]. Bending joined the University of Bath in 1989, first as a Lecturer and then as a Senior Lecturer, from 1995. In 1991–92, Bending supervised [[Andre Geim]] as a postdoc in his group. Geim was subsequently awarded the 2010 Physics Nobel Prize. In 1996, Bending was promoted to Reader and, in 2000, he was appointed to a personal chair in the Department of Physics.

Much of Bending's research evolved from his development of [[scanning Hall probe microscopy]].<ref name="SB1">

==Awards and recognition==
*Elected [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]].
*2002, Mott Prize Lecture at the European Physical Society Condensed Matter meeting, Brighton.
*1999, Royal Society Leverhulme Trust Senior Research Fellowship
*1990, Joint winner of the Philip Morris Prize for Information Technology and Communications, Münich, Germany.
*1984, IBM Student Fellowship at Stanford University, California.
